items.name: Collections Standards
items.summary: Governs how the department pursues and resolves outstanding receivables, from agent balances and reinsurance recoverables to corporate trade debt. Ensures aging balances are surfaced early, escalated consistently, and resolved or written off under controlled authority so receivables remain collectible and accurately stated.

subs.title: Weekly Aging Review
subs.description: The receivables team reviews the full AR aging each week, covering premium receivables, agent and broker balances, and reinsurance recoverables. Balances crossing 30, 60, and 90 day buckets are flagged with a named owner and next action, and the summarized aging is circulated to the Controller for visibility into deteriorating accounts.

subs.title: Dunning Letters per Schedule
subs.description: Past-due accounts receive standardized dunning correspondence on a fixed escalation schedule, with templates and timing approved by Legal and Compliance. For policyholder premium balances, the schedule is coordinated with state-mandated cancellation notice requirements so collection activity never conflicts with regulatory notice periods.

subs.title: Write-Off Approval Matrix
subs.description: Uncollectible balances may only be written off under a documented authority matrix that ties approval level to dollar amount, from receivables manager through Controller to CFO for the largest items. Each write-off requires evidence of collection effort, and aggregate write-off activity is reported quarterly to support bad-debt reserve adequacy.

items.name: Invoice Processing
items.summary: Defines the controlled path every vendor invoice follows from receipt to posting, covering approval, matching, and adherence to negotiated terms. Ensures the carrier pays only for goods and services actually ordered and received, at the agreed price and on the agreed timeline.

subs.title: Invoice Approval Workflow
subs.description: Every invoice is routed through the AP system's electronic approval workflow, with approvers determined by cost center and delegation-of-authority limits. Manual or out-of-system approvals are prohibited, and the workflow preserves a timestamped audit trail of who reviewed and approved each invoice before payment.

subs.title: Three-Way Match for PO Items
subs.description: Invoices tied to purchase orders must match the PO and the goods-receipt or service-acceptance record on quantity and price before they can post. Mismatches outside tolerance are blocked automatically and routed to procurement and the requesting business unit for resolution rather than overridden by AP staff.

subs.title: Payment Terms Enforced
subs.description: Invoices are scheduled for payment according to the contracted vendor terms, neither paid early without Treasury approval nor allowed to slip past due. AP monitors on-time payment performance and captures early-payment discounts where the discount exceeds the carrier's short-term cost of funds.

items.name: Payment Controls
items.summary: Establishes the safeguards applied before funds leave the company, focused on high-value disbursements and changes to payee banking details. Protects the carrier against payment fraud, business email compromise, and unauthorized transfers.

subs.title: Dual Approval for Payments Over $10K
subs.description: Any disbursement exceeding $10,000, whether check, ACH, or wire, requires two independent approvers within the payment system before release. The preparer may not also approve, and approver lists are reviewed quarterly against the delegation-of-authority matrix to confirm limits remain current.

subs.title: Callback Verification for Bank Account Changes
subs.description: Requests to add or change vendor, claimant, or reinsurer bank account details are never actioned from email alone. Treasury staff verify each change by calling a known contact at an independently confirmed phone number on file, documenting the call before the new instructions take effect. This control is the carrier's primary defense against business email compromise schemes targeting claim and premium disbursements.

items.name: External Audit Support
items.summary: Sets the department's obligations for supporting the independent financial statement and statutory audits, from evidence delivery through resolution of auditor observations. Ensures the audit proceeds on schedule and that issues raised are not left open across reporting cycles.

subs.title: PBC List Tracked
subs.description: The prepared-by-client request list from the external auditors is loaded into a shared tracker with an assigned owner and due date for every item. The audit liaison reviews status weekly during fieldwork, covering both GAAP and statutory audit requests, so late or stalled items are escalated before they threaten the audit timeline.

subs.title: 48-Hour Response to Auditor Requests
subs.description: Routine auditor requests and follow-up questions receive a substantive response within two business days. Where the underlying support requires longer to assemble, such as actuarial reserve documentation or investment valuation detail, the owner communicates a committed delivery date within the same 48-hour window.

subs.title: Findings Tracked to Closure
subs.description: Control deficiencies, adjustments, and management letter comments raised by the external auditors are logged with an accountable owner, remediation plan, and target date. Progress is reviewed with the Controller monthly and reported to the Audit Committee until each finding is verified closed, with prior-year items confirmed resolved before the next audit cycle begins.

items.name: Internal Audit Coordination
items.summary: Defines how Finance & Accounting engages with the internal audit function across the audit lifecycle, from planning input through remediation of issues. Ensures internal audit coverage reflects the department's actual risk profile and that its findings produce timely, verifiable corrective action.

subs.title: Annual Audit Plan Input
subs.description: Finance leadership provides a formal risk assessment to internal audit during annual planning, identifying areas of elevated concern such as new accounting standards adoption, system conversions, or processes with recent control changes. This input is documented so the approved plan can be traced back to the risks the department raised.

subs.title: Management Response Within 30 Days
subs.description: When internal audit issues a draft report, the responsible finance manager delivers a written management response within 30 calendar days, either accepting the finding with a remediation plan and date or documenting a substantiated disagreement. Responses are reviewed by the Controller before submission to ensure commitments are realistic and properly resourced.

subs.title: Remediation Tracked
subs.description: Agreed remediation actions are entered into the issue-tracking system with owners and due dates, and status is reported at the department's monthly controls meeting. Items may only be closed once internal audit validates the corrective action, and overdue items are escalated to the CFO.

items.name: Budget Process
items.summary: Governs the construction of the company's annual operating budget across all business lines and corporate functions. Ensures the budget is built on a common timetable and structure and carries explicit executive endorsement before it becomes the baseline for the plan year.

subs.title: Annual Budget Calendar
subs.description: FP&A publishes a budget calendar before the cycle opens, fixing the dates for assumption setting, business unit submissions, challenge sessions, and final approval. The calendar is sequenced so premium, loss, and expense planning across P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits align with actuarial plan-rate timelines and the Board's year-end approval meeting.

subs.title: Standardized Templates
subs.description: All budget submissions use the templates issued by FP&A, with a common chart-of-accounts mapping, consistent expense allocation drivers, and prescribed assumption fields. This uniformity allows submissions from underwriting, claims, and corporate functions to be consolidated and compared without manual restatement.

subs.title: Executive Approval Required
subs.description: The consolidated budget is presented to the executive committee for formal sign-off, and no business unit budget is considered final until that approval is recorded. Subsequent changes to the approved baseline require the same level of authorization, preserving the integrity of variance reporting throughout the year.

items.name: Forecast Standards
items.summary: Establishes the cadence and discipline for the company's financial forecast so leadership always has a current, explained view of expected results. Ensures forecast revisions are timely, forward-looking across a consistent horizon, and supported by clear reasoning for movement against plan.

subs.title: Rolling Four-Quarter Forecast
subs.description: FP&A maintains a forecast that always extends four quarters ahead, crossing fiscal year boundaries rather than truncating at year end. The horizon covers premium production, loss ratios, investment income, and operating expenses by business segment, giving leadership a continuous forward view for capital and reinsurance planning.

subs.title: Monthly Forecast Update
subs.description: The forecast is refreshed every month after the close, incorporating actual results, updated actuarial loss picks, and revised production outlooks from the business units. Each cycle follows a published submission deadline so the consolidated update reaches the CFO before month-end business reviews.

subs.title: Variance Explanation Required
subs.description: Every forecast revision is accompanied by a written explanation of significant movements against both the prior forecast and the annual plan, attributing changes to specific drivers such as catastrophe activity, rate achievement, or expense timing. Unexplained variances above the materiality threshold are returned to the submitting unit before the forecast is accepted.

items.name: Close Calendar
items.summary: Governs the scheduling and monitoring of the monthly and quarterly accounting close so that every contributor works to the same published timetable. Ensures the close completes predictably and that schedule slippage is visible and addressed rather than absorbed silently.

subs.title: Published Standard Close Calendar
subs.description: The Controller's office publishes a close calendar for the full year, assigning a workday-numbered deadline to each activity from subledger cutoff through final consolidation. The calendar coordinates dependencies across actuarial reserve delivery, investment accounting feeds, and intercompany settlement so downstream tasks are never waiting on undefined inputs.

subs.title: Milestone Tracking
subs.description: Key close milestones, including subledger close, reserve booking, and trial balance lock, are tracked in real time during each cycle with completion status visible to the whole close team. The close manager runs brief daily checkpoints during close week to confirm milestones are met or to reassign resources where they are at risk.

subs.title: Variance to Schedule Reported
subs.description: Tasks that miss their calendar deadline are logged with the cause and the recovery action taken, and a schedule-performance summary is included in the post-close review. Recurring slippage in the same activity triggers a root-cause assessment so the calendar or the underlying process is corrected rather than repeatedly missed.

items.name: Close Checklist
items.summary: Requires the close to be executed against a controlled, evidenced checklist rather than individual memory or informal routine. Ensures every required close task is completed, accountably signed off, and supported by retained documentation that can withstand audit scrutiny.

subs.title: Standardized Close Checklist
subs.description: Each entity and ledger closes against a standardized checklist enumerating every required task, from accrual entries and reserve postings to intercompany eliminations and statutory-to-GAAP adjustments. The checklist is maintained centrally by the Controller's office, and additions or removals require its approval so coverage cannot quietly erode.

subs.title: Required Sign-Offs
subs.description: Every checklist task carries a preparer and a separate reviewer sign-off, captured electronically with name and timestamp. The close is not considered complete until all sign-offs are in place, and open items at period end must be formally dispositioned by the assistant controller rather than left blank.

subs.title: Evidence Retained
subs.description: Supporting documentation for each completed checklist task is attached or referenced within the close management tool and retained per the corporate records schedule. The evidence must be sufficient for an external auditor or examiner to reperform the task, including source reports, calculations, and approval trails.

items.name: Journal Entry Controls
items.summary: Establishes the control framework for manual journal entries posted to the general ledger, covering authorization, support, and the integrity of posting dates. Ensures the ledger reflects only properly approved, well-documented entries recorded in the correct accounting period.

subs.title: JE Approval per Authority Matrix
subs.description: Manual journal entries require approval by someone other than the preparer, with the required approval level escalating by entry size under the documented authority matrix. High-dollar and non-routine entries, such as reserve true-ups or impairments, route to the assistant controller or Controller, and the ledger system enforces these thresholds rather than relying on convention.

subs.title: Supporting Documentation
subs.description: Every manual entry is posted with attached support that explains the business purpose and substantiates the amounts, such as calculations, third-party statements, or actuarial memos. An approver who cannot understand and verify the entry from its attached support is required to reject it back to the preparer.

subs.title: No Backdating
subs.description: Entries must be recorded in the period to which they relate while that period is open, and posting into closed periods is prohibited. Once a period is locked, corrections are made through current-period adjusting entries or, for material errors, through a formally approved reopening authorized by the Controller with full documentation of the reason.

items.name: Reconciliation Standards
items.summary: Governs the substantiation of general ledger balances through routine account reconciliation. Ensures every balance sheet account is proven against independent support on a regular cycle and that unresolved differences are visible, aged, and dispositioned according to their significance.

subs.title: Monthly Balance Sheet Reconciliation
subs.description: Every balance sheet account, including premium receivables, loss reserves, reinsurance balances, and investment holdings, is reconciled to its supporting subledger or external source each month. Reconciliations follow a standard format with preparer and reviewer sign-off, and completion status is monitored by the Controller's office against the close calendar.

subs.title: Aging of Reconciling Items
subs.description: Open reconciling items are individually listed with the date they arose and an explanation, and items aging beyond 60 days are escalated to the assistant controller with a resolution plan. Items that cannot be substantiated within 90 days are assessed for write-off or adjustment rather than carried indefinitely.

subs.title: Materiality Thresholds
subs.description: The Controller's office sets documented thresholds that scale reconciliation rigor to account risk and size, defining which accounts require full reperformance versus analytical review and what difference level must be investigated versus noted. Thresholds are reviewed annually and align with the materiality framework agreed with the external auditors.

items.name: SOX Compliance
items.summary: Governs the department's program for maintaining effective internal control over financial reporting under Sarbanes-Oxley. Ensures the key control population is current and documented, tested on a planned cycle, and that identified weaknesses are corrected before they escalate into significant deficiencies or material weaknesses.

subs.title: Key Controls Documented
subs.description: Each key control over financial reporting is documented in the SOX repository with its risk and assertion mapping, control owner, frequency, and evidence requirements, supported by current process narratives and flowcharts. Documentation is refreshed whenever processes or systems change, with an annual certification by control owners that descriptions remain accurate.

subs.title: Testing Calendar
subs.description: Management's control testing follows a published annual calendar that sequences design and operating effectiveness testing across the year and stages high-risk controls early enough to allow remediation and retesting before year end. The calendar is coordinated with internal audit and the external auditors to maximize reliance and avoid duplicate requests on control owners.

subs.title: Timely Deficiency Remediation
subs.description: Control deficiencies identified through testing are logged, rated for severity, and assigned a remediation owner and target date commensurate with risk. Remediation progress is reviewed monthly by the SOX program lead, retesting confirms the fix operated effectively, and open deficiencies are reported to the Disclosure Committee and Audit Committee each quarter.

items.name: Segregation of Duties
items.summary: Governs how the department prevents any single individual from controlling all phases of a financial transaction across initiation, approval, recording, and reconciliation. Ensures duty conflicts are systematically identified across finance systems and either eliminated or covered by documented compensating measures.

subs.title: SOD Matrix Maintained
subs.description: A segregation-of-duties matrix defines incompatible function combinations across the general ledger, accounts payable, treasury, and payroll systems, such as vendor creation paired with payment approval. The matrix is owned by the controls team and updated whenever roles, systems, or processes change, with a full review at least annually.

subs.title: Conflicts Identified and Mitigated
subs.description: User access across financial systems is analyzed against the matrix on a recurring cycle, using automated rule sets where the system supports them. Detected conflicts are removed through role redesign or access changes wherever practical, with particular attention to small treasury and statutory accounting teams where headcount makes conflicts more likely.

subs.title: Compensating Controls Documented
subs.description: Where a duty conflict cannot reasonably be eliminated, a compensating control such as independent secondary review or detailed activity monitoring is designed, documented, and formally accepted by the Controller. Each accepted conflict and its compensating control is recorded in a register and reassessed during the annual SOX scoping exercise.

items.name: Board Reporting
items.summary: Governs the preparation and delivery of financial materials to the Board of Directors and its committees. Ensures directors receive consistent, executive-vetted financial information with enough lead time to fulfill their oversight duties.

subs.title: Board Package Five Days Before Meeting
subs.description: The complete financial section of the board package is distributed through the board portal no fewer than five business days before each meeting. The production timetable works backward from this deadline, and any late-breaking material developments after distribution, such as a major catastrophe loss estimate, are communicated through a formally approved supplement.

subs.title: Standardized Format
subs.description: Board financial reporting follows an approved standing format covering consolidated results, segment performance for P&C, Life & Retirement, and group benefits, capital and RBC position, and investment portfolio summary. Format changes require CFO approval and are introduced with bridging context so directors can follow trends across periods.

subs.title: CFO Review Required
subs.description: The CFO personally reviews and approves all financial content before it is released to directors, confirming accuracy, consistency with reported results, and appropriateness of forward-looking commentary. This review is the final quality gate, and no finance material reaches the board portal without it.

items.name: GAAP Compliance
items.summary: Governs the accounting framework applied to the company's general-purpose financial statements and the discipline around the policies that implement it. Ensures financial reporting rests on consistently applied, well-documented US GAAP positions that change only under controlled executive authority.

subs.title: All Reporting per US GAAP
subs.description: Consolidated and segment financial statements are prepared in conformity with US GAAP, including the insurance-specific guidance governing premium recognition, deferred acquisition costs, loss reserves, and long-duration contract measurement under ASC 944. GAAP results are maintained distinctly from statutory results, with the differences between bases reconciled and understood.

subs.title: Documented Accounting Policies
subs.description: Each significant accounting policy is maintained as a written policy memo stating the authoritative guidance, the company's elected position, and its application to the company's products and transactions. Technical accounting maintains the policy library, assesses new FASB pronouncements for impact, and documents adoption positions before effective dates.

subs.title: Policy Changes Approved by CFO
subs.description: Adoption of new standards, changes in accounting method, and revisions to significant estimates methodology require written CFO approval before implementation, supported by a technical memo analyzing the alternatives. Material changes are also reviewed with the external auditors and disclosed to the Audit Committee before they take effect in reported results.

items.name: Management Reporting
items.summary: Sets the deliverables and timetable for internal financial reporting to company leadership each month. Ensures executives receive an early read on results, a complete profit and loss view on a fixed schedule, and analysis that explains performance rather than merely presenting it.

subs.title: Flash Report by Workday Three
subs.description: A preliminary flash report is issued by the third workday after period end, giving leadership an early estimate of written and earned premium, incurred losses, and headline operating results by segment. The flash draws on preliminary subledger data and actuarial indications, with known open items disclosed so readers understand its provisional nature.

subs.title: Full P&L by Workday Ten
subs.description: The complete management profit and loss package, including segment results, loss and expense ratios, and investment income detail, is published by the tenth workday. This package reflects the final closed ledger and serves as the authoritative basis for monthly business reviews and forecast updates.

subs.title: Variance Analysis Required
subs.description: Management reporting includes written analysis of results against plan, forecast, and prior year, with material variances attributed to specific drivers such as catastrophe losses, prior-year reserve development, rate change, or expense timing. Commentary must explain causes and expected persistence, and FP&A returns submissions that simply restate the numbers.

items.name: Statutory Reporting
items.summary: Governs the preparation and filing of regulatory financial reports for each insurance legal entity with state insurance departments. Ensures statutory obligations across all domiciliary and licensed states are met accurately and on time, protecting the carrier's licenses and standing with regulators.

subs.title: State Statutory Filings per Schedule
subs.description: A consolidated filing calendar tracks every statutory obligation for each insurance entity, including quarterly and annual statements, RBC reports, premium tax returns, and state-specific data calls across all licensed jurisdictions. Each filing has a named owner and internal deadline set ahead of the regulatory due date, with late or amended filings escalated to the Controller.

subs.title: NAIC Compliance
subs.description: Statutory financial statements are prepared in accordance with NAIC statutory accounting principles as codified in the Accounting Practices and Procedures Manual, with any permitted or prescribed practices of the domiciliary states separately identified and disclosed. The statutory accounting team monitors NAIC working group activity and implements changes to SSAPs and annual statement instructions by their effective dates.

subs.title: Annual Statement Accuracy
subs.description: The Annual Statement blank for each entity, including Schedule F reinsurance detail, Schedule P loss development, and the investment schedules, is subject to documented preparation and independent review before officer attestation. Cross-checks and validation against NAIC edits are completed prior to filing, and errors discovered after submission are corrected through prompt amendment with regulator notification.

items.name: Tax Compliance
items.summary: Governs the management of the company's tax filing and payment obligations across federal, state, and local jurisdictions, including insurance-specific levies. Ensures every return and payment is delivered on time or properly extended, avoiding penalties, interest, and regulator attention.

subs.title: Filing Calendar Maintained
subs.description: The tax department maintains a master calendar of every recurring obligation, spanning federal and state income tax returns, premium tax filings in each licensed state, guaranty fund assessments, and information returns. Each item carries an owner, statutory due date, and internal preparation deadline, and the calendar is reconciled annually against the company's licensing footprint to catch new obligations.

subs.title: Extension Requests as Needed
subs.description: Where a return cannot be completed by its original due date, an extension is filed before the deadline under a documented decision by the tax director, accompanied by a payment of the estimated liability to avoid underpayment exposure. Extensions are treated as planned exceptions and tracked to ensure the extended return is filed well within the extension period.

subs.title: Payment Deadlines Met
subs.description: Estimated tax payments, premium tax remittances, and balances due are scheduled in advance with Treasury so funds are positioned and disbursed by each statutory deadline. Payment confirmations are retained, and any penalty or interest notice triggers a root-cause review and abatement request where grounds exist.

items.name: Tax Provision
items.summary: Governs the measurement and reporting of income tax expense in the company's financial statements. Ensures the tax accounts are computed under authoritative guidance each quarter, supported by a credible forward rate view, and that judgmental positions are rigorously documented.

subs.title: Quarterly Provision per ASC 740
subs.description: The income tax provision is prepared each quarter in accordance with ASC 740, applying the estimated annual effective rate method and measuring deferred taxes on temporary differences, including insurance-specific items such as loss reserve discounting and unearned premium adjustments under the tax code. The provision workpapers follow a standard package reviewed by the tax director before results are released to financial reporting.

subs.title: Effective Tax Rate Forecast
subs.description: The tax department maintains a forecast of the annual effective tax rate, updated quarterly for changes in projected pre-tax income mix, tax-exempt investment income, and discrete items. Material movements in the forecast rate are explained to the CFO and incorporated into the financial forecast so earnings guidance reflects a current tax view.

subs.title: Uncertain Tax Positions Documented
subs.description: Tax positions that may not be sustained on examination are identified, evaluated under the more-likely-than-not recognition and measurement framework, and documented in position memos with supporting technical analysis. The uncertain tax position inventory is reassessed each quarter for changes in law, audit activity, and statute expirations, with conclusions reviewed by the external auditors.

items.name: Bank Account Controls
items.summary: Governs the administration of the company's bank account structure across operating, claims disbursement, premium collection, and trust accounts. Ensures Treasury maintains complete and current control over which accounts exist and who can act on them, reducing fraud exposure and reconciliation burden.

subs.title: Bank Account Inventory
subs.description: Treasury maintains a complete register of every bank account held by any company entity, recording the institution, purpose, legal owner, signers, and linked services such as positive pay. New accounts may only be opened through Treasury under documented approval, and the inventory is confirmed against bank records at least annually.

subs.title: Authorized Signers Current
subs.description: Signer authority on every account is kept aligned with current employment and role, with departures and transfers triggering removal from bank records within days, not quarters. A periodic review compares bank-confirmed signer lists to the HR roster and the delegation-of-authority matrix, with discrepancies corrected and reported to the Treasurer.

subs.title: Dormant Accounts Closed
subs.description: Accounts with no business activity over a defined period are reviewed for closure, and those without a justified continuing purpose, such as a state deposit or trust requirement, are closed with residual balances swept to concentration accounts. Closures are documented in the inventory so the account population reflects only what the business actually uses.

items.name: Cash Management
items.summary: Governs the monitoring, forecasting, and positioning of the company's cash so obligations from claim payments to debt service are always funded. Ensures liquidity is visible daily, projected over a meaningful horizon, and held above a protected floor even under stressed claim activity.

subs.title: Daily Cash Position
subs.description: Treasury prepares a consolidated cash position every business morning, capturing prior-day balances and current-day expected flows across operating, claims, and premium accounts. The position drives same-day decisions on funding disbursement accounts, concentrating excess balances, and placing short-term investments.

subs.title: 13-Week Cash Forecast
subs.description: A rolling 13-week forecast projects receipts and disbursements weekly, incorporating premium collection patterns, expected claim payment levels, reinsurance settlements, and scheduled items such as tax payments and dividends. The forecast is refreshed weekly, and forecast-to-actual variances are analyzed to keep projection accuracy improving over time.

subs.title: Minimum Liquidity Maintained
subs.description: The company holds available liquidity at or above a board-approved floor sized to cover stressed outflows, including elevated catastrophe claim payments, without forced sales from the investment portfolio. Treasury monitors headroom against the floor continuously and escalates to the CFO when projections show the buffer compressing, with committed credit facilities counted per the liquidity policy's eligibility rules.

items.name: Investment Policy
items.summary: Governs the management of the company's investment portfolio within the risk boundaries set by the Board and state insurance investment statutes. Ensures the assets backing policyholder reserves and surplus stay within approved exposure and maturity constraints, with results and compliance transparently reported.

subs.title: Investment Policy Compliance
subs.description: All portfolio activity, whether managed internally or by external advisers, must conform to the board-approved investment policy statement covering permitted asset classes, credit quality minimums, and concentration rules, as well as applicable state insurance investment laws. Compliance is tested against holdings on a recurring cycle, and breaches, including passive breaches from downgrades, are escalated and cured within defined timeframes.

subs.title: Counterparty Limits
subs.description: Exposure to any single issuer, counterparty, or guarantor is capped by limits scaled to credit rating and instrument type, aggregating bond holdings, deposits, derivative exposure, and reinsurance collateral arrangements. Limit utilization is monitored as positions and ratings change, and additions that would breach a cap require pre-trade approval or are blocked.

subs.title: Duration Limits
subs.description: Portfolio duration is managed within approved bands set relative to the duration of the underlying liabilities, recognizing the long-tail profile of certain P&C reserves and the long-duration nature of life and annuity obligations. Asset-liability mismatch is measured at the segment level, and positioning outside the bands requires documented approval from the investment committee.

subs.title: Quarterly Investment Reporting
subs.description: Treasury delivers a quarterly report to the investment committee and Board covering portfolio composition, book and market values, investment income, realized and unrealized gains and losses, impairment activity, and policy compliance status. The report also summarizes external manager performance against benchmarks and any policy exceptions granted during the period.
